tweets.body:
We just announced Guide—the industry's first VLSP light engine. Today's lasers are built like lab setups: discrete lenses, epoxy bonds, manual assembly. Instead of scaling bandwidth by bolting on more ELSFPs, we integrated everything into a single photonic chip. 16λ, ±20 GHz wavelength accuracy, powering 100 Tbps of I/O in 1RU.

We're also building out the CPO ecosystem. Announcing partnerships with GUC, Synopsys, and Cadence.

https://t.co/OfrfTkFvqY

tweets.body:
At Lightmatter, we're not just connecting 1 million XPU datacenters together using light. We're committed to ensuring that computational progress continues, even when Moore's Law and Dennard Scaling are gone.

Our publication in @Nature highlights one possible path for computing—using Light. If you love computers, as I do, you will appreciate the historical significance of this result. This is the first non-transistor computer capable of running economically valuable algorithms (not proof-of-life toy problems).

Join the team that is shaping the future of computing.
